VILBERS
Vilber's (VILBERS, vilbers.com) is a Latvian social enterprise that designs and produces adaptive clothing and functional accessories for wheelchair users, made in its own small workshop in Vangaži, Latvia. It sells seated-cut adaptive trousers, jeans, hoodies, T-shirts and blouses, thermal leg covers and footmuffs for winter, breathable raincoats, positioning straps, sleeve protectors and armrest bags, plus outdoor items for children who use wheelchairs or special needs strollers. It is for wheelchair users, people who need assisted dressing, people with limited hand function, and the carers and families who dress them. What sets it apart is that every product started as a request from a real customer, and the clothing is trusted by the Latvian Paralympic team.

Founded in December 2023 in Vangaži, Latvia. Legal entity: Vilbers SIA. The store ships worldwide from Latvia, with free EU delivery on orders over €200. It serves 38 country markets and is available in English, German and French. The store shows 265 customer reviews. Prices on the store are shown in EUR for Latvia and the eurozone, and in local currency in other markets.

1. Company overview
Vilber's began with a childhood memory of its founder, Zane Bērziņa. A close family member used a wheelchair, and she remembers his house full of ramps. As a child she saw no difference between walking and using a wheelchair. He passed away before Vilber's existed, and his memory is where the brand comes from. On the brand's blog, Zane describes herself as a fashion designer with a background in mechatronics.

Founded: December 2023, in Vangaži, Latvia
Legal entity: Vilbers SIA, Reg. No. LV40203526649
Ownership: owned and operated as a family business ("Vilber's ltd." per the FAQ)
Status: official social enterprise status in Latvia (listed in the Ministry of Welfare social enterprise register)
Memberships: Latvian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI); member profile with the Latvian Social Entrepreneurship Association (LSUA)
Team: a small workshop team of four. They are supported by Toms Jankovskis, a wheelchair user who models the products and manages social media.
Production: designed and manufactured in Latvia, European Union
Exports: per Latvian Radio 1 (February 2025), 95% of production is exported to Germany, the UK and the US
Recognition: trusted by the Latvian Paralympic team
Values and approach, as stated on the site
Customer-led design: every product in the collection started as a request from a real customer. The newsletter tagline reads "Every product here started with someone asking for it."
Dignity: garments are designed to look like ordinary everyday clothing without "shouting" their adaptive features.
Fair production: the brand refuses to compromise on garment durability or fair labour, including fair wages and social security for the team.
Independence: the homepage headline is "Independence. Reclaimed."
Focus: the company concentrates only on adaptive clothing, not general sportswear or merchandise.
2. What we sell
The store lists 58 products. The All-in-One Wheelchair Winter Suit is sold on a request-a-quote basis, and gift cards are available.

Adaptive design features used across the range
No-back-seam construction, to remove pressure points and reduce the risk of pressure ulcers
High, elasticated back waist and slightly lowered front, for full coverage and no bunching when seated
Drop-down front panels disguised as side pockets, for easy dressing, toileting and catheter access
Magnetic closures and zips with integrated loops, usable with limited dexterity
Hook-and-loop closures hidden under functional loops
Neoprene bumpers so no metal touches the skin
Adjustable waists that tolerate roughly 20% waist variation if hips and thighs fit
Openable shoulders on T-shirts and fully openable trousers for carer-assisted dressing

Winter
https://vilbers.com/collections/warm-items

Cold-weather gear for wheelchair users. The collection has 12 products, with the All-in-One suit sold on quote. The ThermoShell and Combi products form a modular system: leg covers can be paired with The Base spine-and-bottom wrap for full thermal coverage.

Key products
Wheelchair ThermoShell Racer; 5 reviews, all 5-star
Use: unisex modular leg cover for active users with front-end power add-ons such as Klaxon or SwissTrac. Separate leg sections and side zips with magnetic base.
Outer: Oxford PU 200gsm, 100% polyester, OEKO-TEX Standard 100 certified
Insulation: 3M Thinsulate Type J250 (R-value 3.9, bluesign approved, hypoallergenic)
Lining: polar fleece
Warmth: rated for deep winter, typically -10°C to -20°C with base layers
Colours: Black, Pink, Beige
Lengths: Normal (158–175 cm) and Long (176–190 cm)

Condition-specific collections
Easy closures: clothing for arthritis and limited dexterity. It replaces buttons, small zip pulls and stiff closures with easy-grip zipper loops, magnetic fastenings, hook-and-loop closures and accessible openings, so dressing needs less hand strength.
Sensory friendly: adaptive clothing selection for sensory needs
Prosthetics: adaptive clothing selection for prosthesis users
Down syndrome: adaptive clothing selection for people with Down syndrome

3. Who it is for
Target customers
Manual and power wheelchair users who need clothing cut for a seated position, including paraplegic and quadriplegic users (named in the sizing guide)
People who need assisted dressing, and the carers, family members and care staff who dress them
People with arthritis, limited dexterity or reduced grip strength who benefit from magnetic closures, zip loops and hook-and-loop fastenings
Catheter users who need a drop-down front or wide front opening for toileting and catheterisation
Active wheelchair users with front-end power add-ons (Klaxon, SwissTrac), and users out in extreme weather or doing winter sports
Children who use wheelchairs or special needs strollers such as Hoggi and Otto Bock, and their parents
Healthcare professionals and advocates buying for clients; the affiliate programme targets this group
Use cases and occasions
Everyday wear and leisure wear
Office wear, such as the nettle-fabric blouse and viscose satin set
Winter outdoors down to deep-cold conditions
Rain protection
Hot summer days, with ramie fabric trousers and shorts
School runs and family outings for children
Transfers with a sliding board, supported by smooth-surface fabrics
Protecting sleeves from wheelchair tyre dirt
Keeping legs positioned together in the wheelchair
4. Shipping & delivery
Destinations: worldwide, to the destinations available at checkout
Store markets: 38 countries and regions, listed in section 8
Dispatch: orders are generally prepared and dispatched within 5 business days after confirmation
Delivery time: varies by destination, delivery method and carrier. If Vilbers cannot fulfil an order within the delivery period, the customer is informed.
Delivery methods: parcel lockers, parcel collection points or courier services, depending on the destination
Parcel stations: add the tag PARCELSTATION in the address line plus the chosen parcel station's address
Shipping cost: calculated at checkout based on destination and delivery method
Free shipping: free EU delivery on orders over €200
Customs and taxes: import duties and taxes on international deliveries are the customer's responsibility unless included in the price or collected at checkout
Carriers: specific carrier names are not published on the site
5. Payment methods
American Express, Apple Pay, Bancontact, BLIK, Google Pay, iDEAL Wero, Klarna, Maestro, Mastercard, MobilePay, PayPal, Shop Pay, Union Pay and Visa.

6. Returns, exchanges, warranty
Return window: within two months from the delivery date
Condition: items must be unused
Refund timing: the item cost is refunded within 3 business days of the item arriving at the warehouse; the bank or payment provider may take a few more days
Return shipping: paid by the customer, unless the item is incorrect, damaged or non-conforming, or the law requires otherwise
Return labels: prepaid labels are not provided unless agreed
Exchanges: one free exchange per order, subject to availability
Exclusions: products individually designed and made to individual measurements are not refundable
EU withdrawal right form: https://vilbers.com/a/withdrawal?locale=en
Warranty: no warranty terms are published on the site

9. Reviews, ratings, press, certifications, awards
Reviews
The store-wide review widget (https://vilbers.com/pages/reviews) shows 265 reviews:

5 stars: 235 (89%)
4 stars: 20 (8%)
3 stars: 3 (1%)
2 stars: 3 (1%)
1 star: 4 (2%)
From that distribution, the average is about 4.8 out of 5. Reviews come from customers in the UK, Canada, the US, Germany, the Netherlands and France. They repeatedly mention build quality, fit, and customer service that confirms sizing before shipping.

10. Loyalty, gift cards, B2B/wholesale, subscriptions
Newsletter: 10% off the first order for subscribers. The founder, Zane, writes personally "only when there's something worth sharing." https://vilbers.com/pages/newsletter
Affiliate programme (https://vilbers.com/pages/become-an-affiliate): for advocates, creators and healthcare professionals.
Applications are manually reviewed, with a reply within 3–5 business days.
Approved affiliates get a unique coupon code that gives followers 10% off.
Affiliates earn 5% commission on referred sales, with a 30-day tracking cookie.
Tracking runs through an UpPromote dashboard.
Commissions are paid monthly via PayPal, with a €10 minimum payout.
Apply at https://af.uppromote.com/233d9d-2/register
Gift cards: Vilber's gift card
Wholesale: the contact page handles wholesale enquiries
Custom work: the contact page handles custom adjustments, and some products are made to individual measurements. The All-in-One Wheelchair Winter Suit is sold via request a quote.
Loyalty and subscriptions: no loyalty programme or subscription offer is published
11. Blog
Wheelchair life
https://vilbers.com/blogs/wheelchair-life

Tips on living life to the fullest as a wheelchair user, plus adaptive clothing explainers.

Why quality adaptive clothing costs what it does—and how we can lower it together: Zane Bērziņa (April 2025) explains that costs go to durability and fair labour. She describes how newsletter sign-ups and word-of-mouth cut advertising costs so prices can come down.
Openly about prices: why the price range is what it is; any profit is reinvested in developing new products.
The 10 Most Frequently Googled Questions About Adaptive Clothing: answers to common questions about what adaptive clothing is and how it works.
You don't have the wrong body, you might be lacking the right clothing: the founder's design approach, combining fashion design with a mechatronics background.
Why you should choose adaptive clothing over ordinary garments: the challenges ordinary clothing creates for wheelchair users and people with limited mobility, and how adaptive garments help.
How to date if I am in a wheelchair: dating tips for wheelchair users, including online dating, unhurried conversations and choosing accessible venues.
